title: Exposure Runway Symphony — Checklist & Comms Templates (WIP)
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, cross-functional working doc that treats staged rollout as a "symphony": many small players (telemetry, SRE, product, trust & safety, solutions eng, growth) who need a shared score and a short rehearsal before the first public note. The aim is to provide a minimal checklist, a rehearsal schedule ("human runway"), signal ownership mapping, quick simulation inputs, and usable comms templates so teams can run microreleases / canaries / A/B slices with predictable handoffs.

Status / context:
- Drafted by product-console as an operational sketch for Q1 2025 microrelease runs.
- Intended for feature launches that touch routing, inference models, or behavior changes that can affect user-facing semantics.
- Not a replacement for full incident runbooks; assume SRE and T&S will add their escalation steps.

Quick principles (guiding heuristics):
1) Minimal blast radius: prefer many tiny slices over one big canary.
2) Observable first: do not open exposure until telemetry (metrics + traceable ids) are streaming to dashboards.
3) Human runway: always have a 30–90 minute rehearsal window with stakeholders queued for first lift.
4) Ownership by signal: each key metric has a named owner who can pull the plug.
5) Safe defaults: default rollback path should be simpler than the forward path.

Runway checklist (pre-lift, tick boxes for go/no-go):
- Metrics & dashboards (owner + link):
  - Latency p95/p99 (owner: SRE) — dashboard: /d/latency-canary
  - Unit cost per token (owner: infra/finance) — /d/cost-telemetry
  - Behavioral regressions (owner: Applied-ML/product) — /d/compare-evals
  - Safety signals (owner: T&S) — /d/safety-metrics
  - Error budget and SLO snapshot (owner: SRE) — /d/slo-snapshot
- Canary slice design: percentage, cohort selection, sampling method documented and approved in PRD.
- Routing & fallback configured: explicit fallback policy to previous model or null response.
- Synthetic traffic: small steady synthetic stream reproducing critical flows (sample size and templates attached).
- Playbook & rollback button: active link to the shortcut that reverts traffic, plus communication channel prefixed ~ALL-LAUNCHES.
- Oncall/responder list with phone/pager and 2nd contacts.

Human runway (rehearsal schedule template):
- T-minus 90m: Smoke run with synthetic traffic; confirm dashboards update and alerting behaves.
- T-minus 60m: Stakeholder sync (product, SRE, applied-ML, T&S, growth) — quick checklist readout.
- T-minus 30m: Start canary at 0.5% internal traffic (internal-only cohort if possible). Observe for 20m.
- First decision: keep (move to 2.5%) or revert. Decision captured in decision ledger (see template).
- T-minus 0: If green, progress through ramp steps (2.5% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50%) each with hold windows and owner signoff.

Ramp recipe (example):
- Internal-only 0.5% (20m hold)
- External beta 2.5% (30m hold)
- Customer cohort 10% (60m hold)
- Broad 25% (2h hold)
- Full 100% (after monitoring window and postmortem plan ready)

Decision ledger (copyable line):
- timestamp | stage | metric snapshot link | decision | decision-maker | notes
- 2025-02-03T11:40Z | 2.5% -> 10% hold | /d/compare-evals?snap=20250203-1140 | HOLD | Maya Chen | slight drift in answer length, T&S reviewing

Signal ownership mapping (must be explicit):
- Latency anomalies -> SRE oncall (primary), infra lead (secondary)
- Cost spike (>10% expected) -> infra-finance lead
- Safety-flag increase -> T&S triage lead (pager)
- Model quality regressions (BLEU/ROUGE/LM-eval proxies) -> Applied-ML owner
- User complaints (support tickets) -> CS + solutions-eng liaison

Fallbacks and kill-switch patterns (recommendations):
- Canary quick revert: toggle routing rule to previous model variant (takes <60s) 
- Quarantine routing: divert affected cohort to a sanitized pipeline (no new learned context, read-only)
- Traffic clamp: reduce acceptance rate to 5% while investigating
- Safety escalation: immediate circuit-breaker if T&S signals exceed threshold (auto-rollback enabled)

Comms templates (copiable):
- Slack short alert (channel #launches):
  "[LAUNCH] 11:30 UTC — Starting coalition canary at 0.5% (internal). Owners oncall: @sre-oncall, @applied-ml, @t-and-s. Watch /d/latency-canary and post decisions in #launch-decision-log. If you must stop: post STOP + reason and click revert."

- Post-decision update:
  "[LAUNCH] 12:10 UTC — Decision: HOLD at 2.5%. Reason: spike in flagged responses (T&S). Actions: Applied-ML running quick evals; SRE observing latency. Next checkpoint 12:40 UTC. Decision-maker: Maya Chen."

- Customer-facing downtime/rollback note (template for CS):
  Subject: Temporary rollback of feature X for stability
  Body: We are temporarily rolling back Feature X due to stability checks. Your experience should return to normal within minutes. Contact support@redwood.ai if you notice anything unusual.

Simulation inputs & quick checks (for lab run before real lift):
- Synthetic user mix: 70% read/ summarize, 20% rerank, 10% chat (sample payloads attached in linked doc).
- Token distribution targets: median 120 tokens, 95th 2.5k tokens.
- Concurrency stress: 50 concurrent sessions per replica for smoke test.
- Fault injection scenarios: slow disk, partial KV cache miss, model OOM — observe fallback reactions.

A/B gating heuristics (practical):
- Primary metric must be one of: user engagement delta, safety flags per 1k responses, or error-free response rate.
- Minimum powered sample: 10k impressions per arm for semantic features (lower for latency-only experiments).
- Always run a pre-burn of 24–72 hours to collect baseline distribution before switching variants.

Rehearsal checklist (30m dry run):
- Run synthetic traffic through staged routing with full observability.
- Ensure alert throttles won't hide early noisy signals.
- Confirm chat sessions can be killed mid-conversation without cross-contamination.
- Validate rollback path is faster than forward path (time-to-fully-serve previous model).

Post-mortem & learning capture (template paragraphs):
- Summary: one-paragraph timeline of what happened and why.
- Detection: who first saw the signal and when (timestamped).
- Response: timeline to rollback and mitigation notes.
- Root cause hypotheses and next steps (code, config, test gaps).
- Owners for action items + expected completion dates.

Open questions (to discuss in rehearsal):
- What is an acceptable small drift in generation length before we consider a regression for UX?
- Should synthetic traffic be run from the production ingress path or internal test harness to better exercise routing?
- Can we automate the first two ramp steps while keeping human signoff for larger jumps?

Appendix: quick links & artifacts
- Decision ledger template: (copy to launch doc)
- Synthetic payloads: link to /d/synthetic-payloads-2025-01-15
- Rehearsal calendar grid: proposed slots in Q1 (weekly brown-bag rehearsals)

Notes to self (todo):
- Convert decision ledger into one-click UI action tied to git commit id.
- Add small script to validate safety metric thresholds before lift.
- Ask SRE to expose a single-click revert that also posts the update into Slack automatically.

This is intentionally terse and pragmatic. Feedback welcome — add notes inline, flag missing signal owners, and if you're listed as an owner, please set a primary and secondary contact.
